objective: Make encrypted HTTP point-to-point chat work between two remote PCs on the internet when at least one peer publishes a reachable URL, including NAT-safe reverse delivery.
non_goals: No full mesh or multi-peer rooms
No always-on hosted relay service operated by us
No WebRTC / UDP hole punching stack
No automatic router admin UI beyond optional future UPnP

invariants: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM session crypto and mutual handshake proof-of-possession remain required
Existing endpoints /health, /identity, /handshake, and /message keep working for LAN/direct dial
Tauri commands start_listener, get_status, connect_peer, and send_chat_message remain available
Ciphertext is still rejected unless the sender public key matches the session peer
project.rollback: Revert this branch; peers fall back to LAN-only advertise-127.0.0.1 behavior from the baseline revision.

grill: User need: two remote internet PCs. Pure mutual inbound HTTP fails under typical double-NAT; safest reversible design is reachable-host + mailbox pull for the NATed peer.
Assumed at least one peer can publish a reachable HTTP URL (public IP + port forward, VPS, Tailscale, or tunnel).
Rejected a mandatory central relay for v1 to preserve point-to-point HTTP; mailbox lives on the peer being dialed.

Pre-mortem: most plausible failure is still advertising 127.0.0.1 or requiring dial-back to a NATed peer — mitigate with configurable advertise host, STUN hints, empty listen_url meaning not dialable, and encrypted /pull outbox.
User explicitly requested remote internet PC connectivity; that authorizes optional STUN discovery (external-side-effect) as part of this change.

risk.rationale: Internet-facing HTTP, session auth on pull, encrypted messaging, concurrent poll/send, and optional STUN query to a public server.

acceptance.criterion: Existing LAN two-peer handshake and encrypted exchange tests remain green.
Crypto unit tests including handshake PoP remain green.
When the initiator advertises an unreachable listen_url, the responder can still deliver a reply via outbox pull.
A configured advertise host appears in the published listen URL instead of 127.0.0.1.
acceptance.verification: cd src-tauri && cargo test --test p2p_http advertise_host_used_in_listen_url -- --exact

acceptance.criterion: Tauri backend compiles with the new networking commands.

execution.rationale: Protocol, mailbox, STUN helper, and UI share one integration path on the peer stack.

tasks.outcome: Add advertise host, STUN/local candidates, outbox /pull, and NAT-safe send/poll.
Expose advertise host and shareable URL in the UI; document internet setup.
Validate GraphPact evidence and independent review for the internet path.

evidence.command: cd src-tauri && cargo test --test p2p_http advertise_host_used_in_listen_url -- --exact

findings: Empty listen_url marks peer not dialable; reverse path uses authenticated /pull mailbox.
/pull requires session peer public key and AES-GCM proof over pull-v1.
Advertise host controls share URL; LAN direct /message path preserved.
Residual: still need one reachable peer on the open internet; first-contact TOFU over HTTP; STUN query reveals IP to Google STUN.
